questions.q: According to the lesson, what separates a worthwhile AI project from a demo?
options: It uses the newest and most capable AI tool on the market
You can name whether it creates time, quality, speed or revenue
It runs fully automatically, without anyone reviewing it
It replaces a whole role in the business, not just one task
questions.explain: The lesson says every worthwhile AI project pays off in at least one of four ways (time, quality, speed or revenue), and if you can't name which, you have a demo, not a project.

questions.q: A five-person plumbing company sends quotes but rarely follows up, because nobody has time. Using AI to draft a follow-up for every quote mainly creates which payoff?
options: Time, because it cuts the hours spent writing each quote
Quality, because every quote gets the same structure and terms
Speed, because customers get their first reply within minutes
Revenue, because it adds follow-ups that weren't happening at all
questions.explain: The lesson says revenue usually comes from work that wasn't happening at all, such as follow-ups nobody had time for, so fewer good jobs quietly go cold.

questions.q: A café owner wants to start using AI this month. Which use best fits where the lesson says AI pays off?
options: Drafting replies to common customer emails for staff to check
Letting AI decide next season's menu prices on its own
Having AI handle a difficult conversation with a supplier
Setting up AI for the stock count done twice a year
questions.explain: Drafting is language work AI is strong at, with a person checking before sending; final pricing decisions, relationships and rare tasks are where the lesson says AI doesn't pay off yet.
